newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Clabecq steelworkers reject offer.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Clabecq steelworkers reject offer.

text.p: Workers at bankrupt Belgian steelmaker Forges de Clabecq, which is being considered for a takeover, on Tuesday rejected an early retirement package, Belga news agency said.
In a referendum, 55.7 percent of the voting workers rejected the offer after following trades union advice that the pension payments were too low and there was no guarantee for the future.
Although more than 90 percent of the workers voted in the referendum the result may be disputed because management and some 150 workers did not vote.

The plan aimed to alleviate the consequences of bankruptcy for the workers and make the company attractive for a takeover. Several firms have been mentioned as possible buyers, but the only one to have publicly declared an interest is private Italian-Swiss steel and commodity trader Duferco.
There have been clashes between police and the steelworkers since Clabecq, based in the small town of Tubize near Brussels, was declared bankrupt in January.
The workers are due to meet again on May 15 to discuss future plans.
